info.title: Remote participant API
info.summary: What a black-box solver serves so a coordinator can plan its device(s) with the rest of the house.
info.description: A participant is one device, or a group of devices its own solver plans together (a vendor's EV charger optimiser, EMHASS in another container, a heat pump's controller). The coordinator never sees its model: it asks what-if questions - 'your cheapest plan if your energy cost these prices' - and, once it has chosen, commits one plan. Queries are side-effect free; only a commit changes what the device does. The bodies are the package's JSON Schemas: device-query.v1.json and device-answer.v1.json (interface.query_to_dict / answer_from_dict). The server URL is the API's base, below which /v1/describe and the rest live (an EMHASS serving its devices: http://host:5000/participant). Implemented by home_energy_optimizer.remote: RemoteParticipant (the coordinator's side) and ParticipantService (the solver's, for any HTTP host). Status: draft.

servers.description: the participant, on the local network

get.summary: What this participant is and which questions it answers.

post.summary: A feasible plan with no price given: what it would do uncoordinated (its thermostat, its plan at the import tariff).
Answer one what-if question. MUST NOT change what the device does or will do.
post.description: price_response is the question Dantzig-Wolfe asks - typically a few dozen per plan, so answer in well under a second; its price_draw and price_supply may differ (what drawing costs and supplying is worth at the participant's connection). best_response carries the rest of the house's load (residual_kw): it is sent only to a participant that lists it among its kinds, as it reveals the household's behaviour. proximal is ADMM's step. A horizon the participant cannot plan (another slot length) is 409. A participant that cannot solve answers with a plan it can run and status 'fallback' (the coordinator then proves no bound from it), never with an error.

post.summary: Optional, for a modulating participant: its own plan for a weighted mix of plans it answered.

200.description: The mixed plan, as it would run it.

post.summary: The plan the coordinator chose: run it. The only call with an effect.
post.description: Names the answer chosen by its Query-Id (query_id) and repeats its plan; the participant runs that answer as it gave it, and refuses (409) a query_id it did not answer on this horizon or a plan_kw that is not that answer's.

200.description: Accepted, or refused with a reason (the coordinator then re-plans without it).

QueryId.name: Query-Id
QueryId.description: The coordinator's id for this answer, so a later commit can name the plan it chose.

mutualTLS.description: Preferred on a local network: both ends present certificates (a Matter fabric or EEBus SHIP pairing can issue them).

bearer.description: A token the user pairs once, for participants that cannot do mutual TLS.

key.description: Its name in the coordinator (a device, or devices joined by '+').

max_power_kw.description: The most it can draw or supply in one slot.

modulating.description: A weighted mix of its plans runs as it is (and /v1/blend may be called).

onoff.description: Its plans are on/off schedules: fix it to one plan before re-pricing the others.

kinds.description: The query kinds it answers; price_response is required for Dantzig-Wolfe. Listing best_response agrees to be sent the rest of the house's load.

state_unit.description: The unit of its trajectory (kWh stored, degC, ...).

weights.description: Query-Id -> weight; the weights sum to 1.

plan_kw.description: kW per slot, positive when drawn: the plan to run.

query_id.description: The query it answered, if it is one plan; absent for a blend.

local_price.description: Optional: the price its energy was coordinated at (currency/kWh per slot), for its own fast re-planning.
